evidence: The claim concerns the upstream actions/checkout repository (tag v7 resolving to 3d3c42e5..., and its action.yml inputs). No upstream artifacts were supplied and I have no network access, so I did not run `git ls-remote https://github.com/actions/checkout refs/tags/v7` or read upstream action.yml. Repository files cannot settle this.

Claim concerns the upstream actions/setup-python v7 tag and its action.yml. The repository views contain neither, and I did not query github.com (no network evidence supplied). Not run: git ls-remote https://github.com/actions/setup-python refs/tags/v7 and reading action.yml at that commit.

ci.yml:178-190 pins actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a... # v3 and uses client-id, private-key, permission-pull-requests, outputs token and app-slug. The upstream action.yml at that commit and the v3 tag mapping are not in the repository or supplied artifacts, and no network lookup was run, so the SHA-to-v3 mapping and the input/output names are unverified.

ci.yml:28-29 sets workflow permissions contents: read. The request-review job (ci.yml:141, 155-157) overrides with job-level contents: read and pull-requests: write, and job-level permissions replace workflow defaults under GitHub Actions semantics. The comment step sets GH_TOKEN to the minted App token (ci.yml:185), which is created with permission-pull-requests: write (ci.yml:182). The vendored helper is fetched at run time and is not in the view, so I did not read it. It is invoked with that GH_TOKEN env, so the token it uses follows from the step env.

install-manifest.json line 2 has top-level "artifacts" as an object mapping repo-relative paths to sha256 hashes (lines 3-9); iterating it yields path strings, so test_action_security.py:18 yields owned paths.

Test at tests/unit/test_action_security.py:28-34 calls data.get on each unmanaged .github/**/*.yml. dependabot.yml (top-level version/updates), project-config.yml (top-level mapping keys), and ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml (name/description/labels/body) are all top-level mappings, so .get works; none has a jobs or runs key, so the defaults apply. Remaining unmanaged files are workflows and action.yml, which are mappings by schema; the manifest excludes only the PRFlow-owned ones.

Searched .github for job-level `uses:` (4-space indent): no matches, so no reusable-workflow jobs; job.get('steps', []) is still safe if any appeared. Every `steps:` block (workflows and composite actions) was listed with its first entry; each begins with mapping entries (`- uses:`, `- name:`, `- id:`) or comments before them, so no scalar steps. Test code at tests/unit/test_action_security.py:33-39 and 50-53 therefore does not fail on step.get.

dependency-audit.yml:23 uses actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 (40 lowercase hex) with persist-credentials: false (line 25); line 26 setup-python@ece7cb06caefa5fff74198d8649806c4678c61a1 (40 hex). These are the only uses: entries. dedupe-pr-events/action.yml has no uses: steps (a single bash run step), so it is vacuously compliant. Neither file appears in diff.patch (unchanged). The tests in tests/unit/test_action_security.py:25-54 check exactly these regex/persist-credentials conditions.

tests/unit/test_action_security.py:21-22 returns true if path == owned or owned in path.parents, so a directory entry like .github/actions/read-project-config covers the files inside it. .prflow/install-manifest.json lists 3 action directories (read-project-config, setup-project-env, vendor-plugin) and 3 workflows (devflow.yml, devflow-implement.yml, devflow-retrospective.yml). These match the .github files on disk exactly. The unmanaged dedupe-pr-events action and the other workflows are not exempt and stay checked.

release.yml:72-74 pins pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@7245906fb61fa33a13554f9d5fb856fe61758086 with a '# release/v1' comment and uses packages-dir: dist/. Whether that SHA lies on release/v1 and its action.yml has packages-dir needs the upstream repository, which is not in the supplied views. I did not check it (for example with git ls-remote or the GitHub API).

Mapping pinned SHAs to upstream tags and action.yml inputs requires upstream repository data (docker/*, anchore/sbom-action, actions/attest-build-provenance), which is not in the supplied views. I did not resolve the SHAs against upstream tags or read the upstream action.yml files.

Checking that the pinned SHAs (949feb2, cf430e0, 9000827, efb3536) match upstream v7/v7/v8/v3 tags and action.yml inputs needs upstream repository data. The review supplies none, and I did not run any network lookup such as git ls-remote or an upstream action.yml fetch. The local sources cannot settle this.

The claim concerns the upstream anthropics/claude-code-action repository (whether commit d70510b is the v1 tag and which inputs its action.yml accepts). No upstream data was supplied and I have no network access, so I could not check it. I did not read the workflow's inputs against the upstream action.yml.

Grep of the six workflows in head view found no git push/fetch/tag/notes/pull/commit. Remaining git use is local read-only (security-audit.yml:186-194 git log/diff/show etc.) plus a clone of a public HTTPS URL (security-audit.yml:84). gh usage is 'gh api graphql' / 'gh issue ...', which authenticate via GH_TOKEN, not persisted git config. release.yml:170 uses softprops/action-gh-release (token input) and :72 PyPI publish; docker.yml:83 uses a local path context '.', not a git context. No step relies on persisted checkout credentials.

Grep of all uses: lines in head .github: every unpinned ref (@v6, @v3, @v1, @v7, @v2) is only in manifest-listed files (devflow.yml, devflow-implement.yml, devflow-retrospective.yml, actions/setup-project-env). All other workflows (ci, mcpb, release, docker, security-audit, dependency-audit, close-released-items, move-to-in-progress, sync-pr-status-to-issue) use 40-hex SHAs, and every checkout there has persist-credentials: false. Repo-owned action dedupe-pr-events has no remote uses. Manifest (.prflow/install-manifest.json) lists those exact files/action dirs; tests/unit/test_action_security.py:21-22 skips path==owned or owned in parents, so the exemption works. ci.yml:28-29 workflow permissions contents: read; request-review job (ci.yml:155-157) has contents: read and pull-requests: write.
